sources.entry: Hiddify - Multi-platform proxy client for managing subscriptions and multiple proxy protocols. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/hiddify/hiddify-app) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Hiddify is a multi-platform proxy client built on the Sing-box toolchain for managing subscriptions and connecting through many proxy protocols.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Hiddify as a proxy client based on the Sing-box universal proxy tool-chain, offering automatic node selection, TUN mode, and remote profiles. It supports protocols such as Vless, Vmess, Reality, TUIC, Hysteria, Wireguard, and SSH. It imports subscription links and configurations in Sing-box, V2ray, Clash, and Clash Meta formats, and updates subscriptions automatically. Profile details such as remaining days and traffic usage are shown in the app. The README lists Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux as supported platforms, and says it is ad-free and open source. Installation links for each platform and tutorials are on a linked wiki page.
use_cases: access the internet through a proxy
connect using Vless, Vmess, or Hysteria protocols
run a VPN-style tunnel with TUN mode
automatically pick the fastest proxy node
use one proxy client across phone and desktop
how_to_run: Download the app for your platform from the Direct Download section or the official stores listed in the README
Follow the installation tutorials on the project wiki linked from the README
Add a subscription link or configuration in the app
Select a node or let automatic node selection choose one
notable: Built on the Sing-box proxy toolchain
Supports many protocols including Reality, TUIC, Hysteria, and Wireguard
Accepts Sing-box, V2ray, Clash, and Clash Meta subscription formats
Delay-based node selection and automatic subscription updates
Ships configuration tuned for Iran, China, and Russia
caveats: The README does not state a license
Setup and usage depend on external subscription providers or panels
Installation details are on an external wiki rather than in the README
